name: Big 30: 120 example answers
description: Four answers for each original question, with recall cues, useful chunks, follow-up replies and reusable prompts.

items.title: Tell me about yourself. — Original website example
items.cue: Tell me about yourself.
items.model: I’m a product designer with five years of experience. I mainly work on mobile apps, and I enjoy turning complicated problems into simple experiences.
expressions: I’m currently…
Most of my experience is in…
Outside of work…

challenge.cue: What got you interested in that?

items.title: Tell me about yourself. — Office worker and beginner cook
items.cue: Tell me about yourself.
items.model: I'm currently working in customer service for a small online shop. Most of my day involves answering questions and helping people with their orders. I used to be quite shy, but this job has made me more comfortable talking to strangers. Outside of work, I enjoy cooking. I'm trying to learn one new dish each month, although my first curry was far too spicy.
expressions: I'm currently working in = my present job is
most of my day involves = I spend much of my day doing
outside of work = during my free time

challenge.cue: What got you interested in that?
challenge.model: I started cooking because I wanted to spend less on takeaway meals. Then I realised I actually enjoyed experimenting with flavours.

items.title: Tell me about yourself. — Student exploring a career
items.cue: Tell me about yourself.
items.model: I'm a business student, and I'm in my final year. At the moment, I'm helping with a student event, which has given me a chance to practise organising things and talking to different people. I'm interested in marketing, but I'm still exploring my options. In my free time, I play badminton with friends. We aren't very competitive; we mainly go for the company.
expressions: at the moment = right now
given me a chance to = allowed me to
exploring my options = considering different choices

challenge.cue: What got you interested in that?
challenge.model: A class project got me interested in marketing. I liked finding out why people choose one product over another.

items.title: Tell me about yourself. — Career change and family life
items.cue: Tell me about yourself.
items.model: I recently moved into administrative work after spending several years in retail. I help a small team organise appointments and keep track of documents. The routine is quite different, so I'm still getting used to it. I live with my family, and we usually have dinner together. One thing I'd like to do this year is become more confident speaking English on the phone.
expressions: moved into = changed to a new field
keep track of = stay aware of and organised about
getting used to = becoming familiar with

challenge.cue: What got you interested in that?
challenge.model: I liked helping customers in retail, but I wanted more regular hours. A friend suggested looking into administrative roles.

items.title: Why are you learning English? — Original website example
items.cue: Why are you learning English?
items.model: I’m learning English because I want to contribute more confidently in international meetings. It also helps me build stronger relationships with colleagues and customers.
expressions: I’m learning English because…
The situation I find hardest is…
My goal is to…

challenge.cue: When do you most need to use English?

items.title: Why are you learning English? — Speaking in work meetings
items.cue: Why are you learning English?
items.model: I'm learning English because I want to take a more active part in meetings. I can usually understand the discussion, but I sometimes spend so long planning a sentence that I miss my chance to speak. My goal is to give a clear update without reading a script. At the moment, I record a short answer each evening and practise a few useful phrases.
expressions: take a more active part in = participate more
miss my chance to = lose an opportunity to
without reading a script = using my own words

challenge.cue: When do you most need to use English?
challenge.model: I need it most during our weekly team meeting, especially when someone asks an unexpected question about my work.

items.title: Why are you learning English? — Independent travel
items.cue: Why are you learning English?
items.model: I want to feel more independent when I travel. Last year, I had trouble explaining a booking problem, and I had to ask my friend to speak for me. I'd like to handle situations like that myself. I'm starting with hotel, restaurant and transport conversations. I practise both sides out loud so that I can respond instead of only memorising my own question.
expressions: feel more independent = need less help
had trouble explaining = found it difficult to explain
handle situations = deal with what happens

challenge.cue: When do you most need to use English?
challenge.model: I mainly need English at hotels and transport counters, where I have to explain a problem or understand instructions.

items.title: Why are you learning English? — Friendship and conversation
items.cue: Why are you learning English?
items.model: I'm learning English because I'd like to connect with more people. Some of my friends are more comfortable speaking English, and I often stay quiet when the conversation gets lively. I don't need to sound perfect. I just want to share a story and ask natural follow-up questions. I've started sending short voice messages to a friend who is happy to practise with me.
expressions: connect with = build a relationship with
more comfortable speaking = find it easier to speak
I've started = I recently began

challenge.cue: When do you most need to use English?
challenge.model: I use it most when I'm having lunch with friends. Keeping up with a relaxed group conversation is my biggest challenge.

items.title: What do you do for a living? — Original website example
items.cue: What do you do for a living?
items.model: I work in product design. I research what users need, create prototypes, and work with engineers to improve the final product.
expressions: I work in…
My main responsibility is…
At the moment…

challenge.cue: What do you enjoy most about it?

items.title: What do you do for a living? — Retail worker
items.cue: What do you do for a living?
items.model: I work in a clothing shop. My main responsibility is helping customers find something that fits their needs and budget. I also organise new stock and check that the shelves are tidy. At the moment, I'm learning how to handle returns on my own. I like the variety because no two customers ask exactly the same questions.
expressions: my main responsibility is = my most important duty is
on my own = without help
at the moment = currently

challenge.cue: What do you enjoy most about it?
challenge.model: I enjoy helping someone find an item they feel comfortable wearing, especially when they arrived unsure about what they wanted.

items.title: What do you do for a living? — Software developer
items.cue: What do you do for a living?
items.model: I'm a software developer at a small company. I build and improve features on a website that customers use to place orders. A lot of my work involves checking why something isn't working and finding a practical fix. Right now, I'm making the checkout process easier to use. I work closely with a designer, so we discuss small details quite often.
expressions: a lot of my work involves = I often work on
finding a practical fix = solving something in a useful way
work closely with = cooperate regularly with

challenge.cue: What do you enjoy most about it?
challenge.model: I enjoy the moment when a confusing problem starts to make sense and I can turn it into a clear solution.

items.title: What do you do for a living? — Currently between jobs
items.cue: What do you do for a living?
items.model: I'm between jobs at the moment. I previously worked as an office assistant, helping with appointments, documents and customer enquiries. I'm now looking for a similar role with more opportunities to learn. While I apply, I'm taking a short spreadsheet course and practising my English. Having a small daily routine helps me feel that I'm moving forward.
expressions: between jobs = not employed while moving to another job
previously worked as = had this job before
moving forward = making progress

challenge.cue: What do you enjoy most about it?
challenge.model: In my previous role, I most enjoyed making things easier for the team, such as organising information so everyone could find it quickly.

items.title: What do you do outside of work? — Original website example
items.cue: What do you do outside of work?
items.model: Outside work, I enjoy cooking, walking, and meeting friends for coffee. These activities help me slow down and recharge.
expressions: Outside of work, I enjoy…
I got into it because…
Recently, I…

challenge.cue: How did you get interested in that?

items.title: What do you do outside of work? — Walking and photography
items.cue: What do you do outside of work?
items.model: Outside of work, I enjoy walking and taking photos on my phone. I usually go to a nearby park twice a week, especially after a busy day. I like noticing small things that I'd normally walk past. Last Sunday, I spent nearly ten minutes trying to photograph a bird that wouldn't stay still. The picture wasn't great, but I enjoyed the walk.
expressions: outside of work = in my free time
I'd normally = I would usually
spent nearly ten minutes = used almost ten minutes

challenge.cue: How did you get interested in that?
challenge.model: I started taking photos during my walks because I wanted a reason to slow down and pay attention to what was around me.

items.title: What do you do outside of work? — Cooking with family
items.cue: What do you do outside of work?
items.model: I enjoy cooking with my family when I have time. We usually make one meal together at the weekend, and everyone takes a different task. I'm normally responsible for chopping vegetables because I'm still learning the more difficult parts. Recently, we made dumplings, and mine looked rather unusual. They tasted fine, though, so I counted that as a success.
expressions: when I have time = when I am available
responsible for = the person doing a task
counted that as = considered that to be

challenge.cue: How did you get interested in that?
challenge.model: My mother invited me to help one weekend. I enjoyed talking while we cooked, so it gradually became something we did regularly.

items.title: What do you do outside of work? — Quiet hobbies
items.cue: What do you do outside of work?
items.model: Most evenings, I like to read or play a puzzle game. My job involves talking to people all day, so I enjoy having some quiet time afterwards. I usually read a few pages before bed rather than setting a strict target. Recently, I finished a mystery novel that kept me guessing until the end. I've already borrowed another book by the same writer.
expressions: quiet time = time without much noise or conversation
rather than = instead of
kept me guessing = made the answer difficult to predict

challenge.cue: How did you get interested in that?
challenge.model: A friend lent me a short mystery novel a few years ago. Finishing it gave me the confidence to try longer books.

items.title: How was your weekend? — Original website example
items.cue: How was your weekend?
items.model: My weekend was quiet but good. I tried a new restaurant on Saturday, then spent Sunday preparing for the week.
expressions: It was pretty…
I spent most of it…
The best part was…

challenge.cue: Do you have anything planned for next weekend?

items.title: How was your weekend? — Relaxing weekend
items.cue: How was your weekend?
items.model: It was pretty relaxing. I spent Saturday morning doing a few chores, and then I met a friend for lunch. We found a small café that serves really good soup. On Sunday, I stayed home and watched a film with my family. Nothing particularly exciting happened, but that was exactly what I needed after a busy week. I felt more rested by Monday.
expressions: it was pretty relaxing = it was quite restful
spent Saturday morning = used that part of Saturday
exactly what I needed = suited my needs very well

challenge.cue: Do you have anything planned for next weekend?
challenge.model: I might visit my cousin next weekend, but we haven't fixed a time yet. I'd also like to leave one afternoon free.

items.title: How was your weekend? — Busy but enjoyable weekend
items.cue: How was your weekend?
items.model: My weekend was busy but enjoyable. I helped my sister move into her new flat on Saturday. We thought it would take two hours, but we were still carrying boxes in the evening. The best part was eating takeaway on the floor afterwards because her table hadn't arrived. I spent Sunday recovering and catching up on the washing.
expressions: helped my sister move = assisted with changing homes
the best part was = the most enjoyable moment was
catching up on = doing something that had been delayed

challenge.cue: Do you have anything planned for next weekend?
challenge.model: Next weekend, I'm planning something much quieter. I might go for a short walk, but I don't want to organise anything complicated.

items.title: How was your weekend? — Plans changed by rain
items.cue: How was your weekend?
items.model: It didn't go quite as planned, but it turned out well. We wanted to have a picnic, and then it rained heavily all morning. Instead, everyone came to my place and brought something to eat. We played a board game and talked for hours. I was disappointed at first, but staying inside actually gave us more time to catch up.
expressions: didn't go quite as planned = happened differently from expected
turned out well = had a good result
catch up = share news after time apart

challenge.cue: Do you have anything planned for next weekend?
challenge.model: We may try the picnic again if the weather is better. Otherwise, I'm happy to do another simple meal at home.

items.title: What are your long-term goals? — Original website example
items.cue: What are your long-term goals?
items.model: My long-term goal is to lead a product team. I’m building my communication skills now because clear leadership depends on clear communication.
expressions: In the long term, I’d like to…
What matters to me is…
Right now, I’m…

challenge.cue: What is the next small step?

items.title: What are your long-term goals? — Growing at work
items.cue: What are your long-term goals?
items.model: In the long term, I'd like to manage a small team. I enjoy solving problems, but I also like helping other people feel confident in their work. Right now, I'm learning how to give clearer updates and feedback. I don't have a fixed deadline for getting a management role. I'd rather build the right skills than move too quickly and feel unprepared.
expressions: in the long term = over the next several years
I'd like to = I hope to
build the right skills = develop useful abilities

challenge.cue: What is the next small step?
challenge.model: My next step is to ask my manager whether I can help a new colleague settle in and learn our usual processes.

items.title: What are your long-term goals? — Balanced personal life
items.cue: What are your long-term goals?
items.model: My long-term goal is to build a life that feels stable without becoming too predictable. I'd like to have work I enjoy, enough savings for unexpected expenses, and time for my family. At the moment, I'm reviewing my spending and trying to protect one evening a week for rest. I know my priorities may change, so I check whether my plans still suit me.
expressions: at the moment = currently
unexpected expenses = costs I did not plan for
my priorities may change = different things may become important

challenge.cue: What is the next small step?
challenge.model: I'm going to look at my usual weekly schedule and choose one commitment I can simplify, so I have more time for family.

items.title: What are your long-term goals? — Small business idea
items.cue: What are your long-term goals?
items.model: I'd eventually like to run a small baking business. I enjoy making cakes, and I'd like to see whether I could turn that interest into regular work. For now, I'm practising a few recipes and keeping track of the ingredients I use. I'm not planning to leave my job immediately. I want to learn more and test the idea before making a big decision.
expressions: I'd eventually like to = I hope to do this later
for now = at the present stage
keep track of = record and monitor

challenge.cue: What is the next small step?
challenge.model: I'll choose one cake recipe and make it several times, so I can see whether I can produce a consistent result.

items.title: What got you interested in your career? — Original website example
items.cue: What got you interested in your career?
items.model: I became interested in my career after helping redesign a student website. I liked combining creativity with practical problem-solving.
expressions: I first became interested when…
What attracted me was…
That led me to…

challenge.cue: Would you choose the same career again?

items.title: What got you interested in your career? — Technology interest
items.cue: What got you interested in your career?
items.model: I first became interested in technology when my uncle asked me to help update his shop's website. I didn't know much, so I followed tutorials and asked a lot of questions. What attracted me was seeing a small change make the site easier to use. That experience led me to study web development and eventually apply for a junior role.
expressions: first became interested when = my interest began at that time
what attracted me was = what I found appealing was
led me to = caused me to take the next step

challenge.cue: Would you choose the same career again?
challenge.model: I probably would choose it again because I still enjoy solving practical problems. I would ask for guidance earlier, though.

items.title: What got you interested in your career? — Helping people learn
items.cue: What got you interested in your career?
items.model: I became interested in teaching when I helped a younger cousin prepare for an exam. At first, I thought teaching meant explaining everything clearly. Then I realised I also had to understand where she was getting confused. I enjoyed finding a different example that finally made sense to her. That experience encouraged me to volunteer as a tutor and learn more about education.
expressions: at first = in the beginning
made sense to her = became understandable to her
encouraged me to = gave me motivation to

challenge.cue: Would you choose the same career again?
challenge.model: Yes, I think I would. I still find it rewarding when someone gains confidence, although I've learned that the work also takes patience.

items.title: What got you interested in your career? — Unexpected career path
items.cue: What got you interested in your career?
items.model: I didn't plan to work in logistics. I took an administrative job at a delivery company because it was close to home. Over time, I became interested in how all the different steps fitted together. I liked finding out why a parcel was delayed and helping the team solve the problem. Eventually, I asked to learn more about planning deliveries and moved into that area.
expressions: over time = gradually
fitted together = worked as parts of a whole
moved into that area = changed to that type of work

challenge.cue: Would you choose the same career again?
challenge.model: I would, although I'd learn more about the field before starting. Understanding the whole process would have helped me settle in faster.

items.title: Do you prefer working from home or the office? — Original website example
items.cue: Do you prefer working from home or the office?
items.model: I prefer a mix of home and office work. Home is good for focused tasks, while the office makes collaboration and quick decisions easier.
expressions: I generally prefer…
The main reason is…
That said…

challenge.cue: What kind of work is easier in the office?

items.title: Do you prefer working from home or the office? — Preference for home
items.cue: Do you prefer working from home or the office?
items.model: I generally prefer working from home when I need to concentrate. I can start earlier because I don't spend time commuting, and it's easier to avoid interruptions. That said, I sometimes miss the quick conversations that happen in the office. My ideal arrangement would be mostly home working, with one or two office days for planning and catching up with the team.
expressions: I generally prefer = I usually choose
that said = despite what I just mentioned
my ideal arrangement would be = the setup I would like most is

challenge.cue: What kind of work is easier in the office?
challenge.model: Brainstorming and helping a new colleague are usually easier in the office because we can ask questions and explain things immediately.

items.title: Do you prefer working from home or the office? — Preference for office
items.cue: Do you prefer working from home or the office?
items.model: I prefer working in the office because I like having a clear separation between work and home. When I leave the building, it's easier to switch off. I also find it simpler to ask a quick question in person. Working from home is useful when I need quiet time, though. For me, an office-based week with occasional home days would work well.
expressions: clear separation between = a distinct boundary between
switch off = stop thinking about work
in person = face to face

challenge.cue: What kind of work is easier in the office?
challenge.model: Tasks that need lots of short discussions are easier in the office. I can check a detail without arranging a separate call.

items.title: Do you prefer working from home or the office? — Experience limited to study
items.cue: Do you prefer working from home or the office?
items.model: I haven't had a job that offered both options, but I've studied at home and on campus. Based on that, I think I'd prefer a mix. Home is comfortable for reading and writing, while being around other people helps me stay motivated. I'd want to try both before making a firm choice, especially because the team and the type of work would matter.
expressions: based on that = using that experience as a guide
a firm choice = a definite decision
the type of work would matter = the tasks would affect my preference

challenge.cue: What kind of work is easier in the office?
challenge.model: I'd expect group planning and practical training to be easier in the office, but I'd need some experience to know for sure.

items.title: What are you currently working on? — Original website example
items.cue: What are you currently working on?
items.model: I’m currently working on a checkout redesign. Our goal is to reduce confusion and help customers complete their orders more easily.
expressions: I’m currently working on…
At the moment…
The next step is…

challenge.cue: What is the biggest challenge?

items.title: What are you currently working on? — Work task update
items.cue: What are you currently working on?
items.model: I'm currently working on a clearer FAQ page for our customers. We keep receiving the same questions about delivery, so the aim is to make the answers easier to find. I've collected the common questions and written a first draft. The tricky part is keeping the information simple without leaving out important details. Next, I'll ask a colleague to check it before we publish it.
expressions: currently working on = doing this task now
the aim is to = the purpose is to
the tricky part is = the difficult part is

challenge.cue: What is the biggest challenge?
challenge.model: The biggest challenge is choosing what to include. I want the page to answer real questions without becoming too long to read.

items.title: What are you currently working on? — Personal learning task
items.cue: What are you currently working on?
items.model: I'm working on improving my spoken English. More specifically, I'm preparing answers to common questions so I don't freeze when someone asks about my life. I've started with introductions and weekend conversations. My main challenge is speaking without reading every sentence. My next step is to reduce each answer to a few keywords and try recording it again.
expressions: more specifically = to describe it more precisely
I've started with = my first focus has been
my next step is = what I will do next is

challenge.cue: What is the biggest challenge?
challenge.model: The hardest part is trusting that I can explain the idea with simple words instead of remembering the exact sentence I wrote.

items.title: What are you currently working on? — Home organisation task
items.cue: What are you currently working on?
items.model: At the moment, I'm sorting out a spare room so it can become a study area. I've cleared most of the boxes and measured the space for a desk. The main difficulty is deciding what to keep because some things have personal value. Next, I'm going to organise the books and choose a chair that fits the room.
expressions: at the moment = right now
sorting out = organising or dealing with
the main difficulty is = the biggest challenge is

challenge.cue: What is the biggest challenge?
challenge.model: Deciding what to keep takes the most time. I'm trying to separate things I actually use from things I only keep out of habit.

items.title: Tell me about your hometown. — Original website example
items.cue: Tell me about your hometown.
items.model: My hometown is a busy coastal city known for its food. I like that it feels energetic, but friendly at the same time.
expressions: I’m from…
It’s known for…
What I like most is…

challenge.cue: How has it changed?

items.title: Tell me about your hometown. — Coastal hometown
items.cue: Tell me about your hometown.
items.model: I'm from a small town near the coast. It's known locally for its seafood, but what I remember most is the relaxed atmosphere. My family used to walk along the water in the evening and buy something simple for dinner. I don't live there now, but I still visit when I can. Going back usually makes me slow down a little.
expressions: I'm from = my home place is
what I remember most is = my strongest memory is
used to walk = walked regularly in the past

challenge.cue: How has it changed?
challenge.model: There are more cafés and visitors now. Some streets are busier, but the area near my old home still feels familiar.

items.title: Tell me about your hometown. — Busy city neighbourhood
items.cue: Tell me about your hometown.
items.model: I grew up in a busy part of Kuala Lumpur. There were shops, food stalls and buses nearby, so it was easy to get around without planning much. It could be noisy, especially in the evening, but I liked having people around. My favourite memory is going downstairs for breakfast with my father and seeing the same stall owners every weekend.
expressions: get around = travel from place to place
people around = other people nearby
my favourite memory is = one experience I remember fondly is

challenge.cue: How has it changed?
challenge.model: There are more tall buildings now, and some old shops have closed. I still recognise the streets, but the pace feels faster.

items.title: Tell me about your hometown. — Quiet inland town
items.cue: Tell me about your hometown.
items.model: My hometown is a quiet inland town surrounded by hills. It isn't somewhere most tourists would think of visiting, but it has a strong community feeling. When I was growing up, people often recognised my family at the market. What I like most is the slower pace. I enjoy city life too, but I miss being able to walk outside and see so much greenery.
expressions: surrounded by = with something all around
what I like most is = my favourite feature is
slower pace = a less hurried way of living

challenge.cue: How has it changed?
challenge.model: The centre has become busier, and there are a few new housing areas. The hills nearby still look much the same to me.

items.title: What is a skill you want to learn? — Original website example
items.cue: What is a skill you want to learn?
items.model: I want to learn public speaking. It would help me explain ideas clearly and feel calmer when presenting to a group.
expressions: I’d like to learn…
It would help me…
I’ve started by…

challenge.cue: What would success look like?

items.title: What is a skill you want to learn? — Learning to cook
items.cue: What is a skill you want to learn?
items.model: I'd like to learn how to cook a few meals confidently. At the moment, I can manage noodles and eggs, but I rely on takeaway more than I'd like. Cooking would help me spend less and choose what goes into my food. I've started by practising one simple recipe each weekend. My first target is to make dinner for my family without feeling stressed.
expressions: I'd like to learn how to = I want to develop the ability to
rely on = depend on
I've started by = my first action has been

challenge.cue: What would success look like?
challenge.model: Success would mean being able to prepare three or four reliable meals without checking every step in a recipe.

items.title: What is a skill you want to learn? — Learning to swim
items.cue: What is a skill you want to learn?
items.model: I want to learn to swim properly. I can move a little in shallow water, but I don't feel confident. I'd like to enjoy the pool with my friends instead of sitting at the side. I'm planning to join a beginner class and learn at a steady pace. I'm less interested in swimming fast than in feeling comfortable with the basic movements.
expressions: feel confident = trust my ability
at a steady pace = gradually and consistently
less interested in = not as focused on

challenge.cue: What would success look like?
challenge.model: For me, success would be swimming a short distance comfortably in a supervised pool and knowing how to stop and rest safely.

items.title: What is a skill you want to learn? — Learning presentations
items.cue: What is a skill you want to learn?
items.model: I'd like to get better at giving short presentations. I know my work quite well, but I become nervous when everyone is looking at me. It would help me explain my ideas more clearly. I've started by recording two-minute updates and listening for places where I lose the main point. Next, I'd like to practise in front of one supportive colleague.
expressions: get better at = improve a skill
the main point = the most important message
in front of = with someone watching or listening

challenge.cue: What would success look like?
challenge.model: I'd like to explain one idea clearly for a few minutes and answer a simple question without feeling that I need a complete script.

items.title: Describe a typical workday. — Original website example
items.cue: Describe a typical workday.
items.model: I usually start by checking priorities and messages. I spend most of the day designing, reviewing work, and meeting with my team.
expressions: I usually start by…
Most of my time goes into…
Before I finish…

challenge.cue: Which part of the day is most demanding?

items.title: Describe a typical workday. — Office routine
items.cue: Describe a typical workday.
items.model: I usually start by checking my calendar and choosing the most important task for the morning. Most of my time goes into preparing documents and answering enquiries. The afternoon is less predictable because people often need help with urgent requests. Before I finish, I check what is still open and leave myself a short note for tomorrow. That makes the next morning easier.
expressions: I usually start by = my normal first action is
most of my time goes into = I spend much of my time on
before I finish = near the end of my day

challenge.cue: Which part of the day is most demanding?
challenge.model: The afternoon is usually the most demanding because I need to respond to other people while still finishing my own tasks.

items.title: Describe a typical workday. — Shop routine
items.cue: Describe a typical workday.
items.model: My workday starts before the shop opens. I check the shelves, tidy the counter and find out whether any new stock is arriving. Once customers come in, I spend most of my time helping them and handling payments. Lunchtime can be particularly busy. At the end of the shift, I help tidy up and pass any important information to the next person.
expressions: once customers come in = after shoppers arrive
at the end of = during the final part of
pass information to = tell the next person what they need to know

challenge.cue: Which part of the day is most demanding?
challenge.model: Lunchtime is the busiest part because several customers may need help at once. I have to stay polite and keep track of the queue.

items.title: Describe a typical workday. — Study day instead of paid work
items.cue: Describe a typical workday.
items.model: I'm studying full-time, so my typical weekday is organised around classes rather than a job. I usually review my notes in the morning and attend lessons later in the day. Between classes, I work on assignments or meet classmates for group tasks. The timing changes from day to day. Before dinner, I try to decide what needs my attention tomorrow.
expressions: organised around = planned according to
rather than = instead of
from day to day = on different days

challenge.cue: Which part of the day is most demanding?
challenge.model: The most demanding part is usually the gap between classes when I need to switch quickly from listening to working on an assignment.

expressions: especially when = particularly in that situation
the memory is part of it = the experience also explains my preference
without rushing = at a comfortable pace

challenge.cue: Can you cook it yourself?
challenge.model: I can prepare the filling and fold them, although mine don't look very neat. I'm getting better at sealing the edges properly.

items.title: How do you stay productive? — Original website example
items.cue: How do you stay productive?
items.model: I stay productive by choosing three priorities and protecting time for focused work. I also take short breaks before my attention drops.
expressions: What helps me most is…
I usually prioritise…
If I fall behind…

challenge.cue: Which habit has the biggest effect?

items.title: How do you stay productive? — Three priorities
items.cue: How do you stay productive?
items.model: What helps me most is choosing three important tasks before I open my messages. That gives me a direction instead of immediately reacting to everything. I usually prioritise the task with the nearest real deadline. I put my phone away during a short work session and then check messages afterwards. If I fall behind, I adjust the list rather than trying to force everything into the evening.
expressions: what helps me most is = my most useful method is
if I fall behind = if I make less progress than planned
rather than trying = instead of attempting

challenge.cue: Which habit has the biggest effect?
challenge.model: Putting my phone away has the biggest effect. It removes the small interruptions that make an ordinary task take much longer.

items.title: How do you stay productive? — Small starting step
items.cue: How do you stay productive?
items.model: I stay productive by making the first step very small. If I write down something vague like finish the project, I tend to put it off. Instead, I choose an action such as write the opening paragraph or check five records. Once I've started, it's easier to continue. When the day changes unexpectedly, I choose a new small step that still moves the important work forward.
expressions: put it off = delay doing it
once I've started = after beginning
moves the work forward = makes useful progress

challenge.cue: Which habit has the biggest effect?
challenge.model: Writing a clear first action helps me most. It reduces the time I spend deciding where to begin.

items.title: How do you stay productive? — Flexible study routine
items.cue: How do you stay productive?
items.model: I plan my study around the times when I can concentrate best. I usually do the hardest reading in the morning and save simpler tasks for later. Before starting, I put the materials I need on my desk and close unrelated tabs. If a topic takes longer than expected, I move a less important task. The plan helps me, but I don't expect every day to look exactly the same.
expressions: around the times when = according to when
longer than expected = requiring more time than planned
less important task = a lower-priority activity

challenge.cue: Which habit has the biggest effect?
challenge.model: Preparing the desk before I start helps a lot. If everything is ready, I have fewer reasons to interrupt myself.

items.title: Who has influenced you? — Original website example
items.cue: Who has influenced you?
items.model: A former manager influenced me because she gave clear feedback without making people defensive. I try to use the same approach with others.
expressions: Someone who influenced me is…
What I admire is…
Because of that…

challenge.cue: Have you told them?

items.title: Who has influenced you? — Patient teacher
items.cue: Who has influenced you?
items.model: A teacher at school influenced me because she made it feel safe to ask questions. Once, I gave an answer that was completely wrong, and she asked me to explain how I'd reached it instead of dismissing it. We found the misunderstanding together. Because of that experience, I try to be patient when someone asks me something basic. They may be making a real effort to understand.
expressions: made it feel safe to = helped me feel comfortable doing
reached it = arrived at that answer
because of that experience = as a result of what happened

challenge.cue: Have you told them?
challenge.model: I thanked her before leaving school, but I didn't explain the full effect at the time. I'd like to do that if we meet again.

items.title: Who has influenced you? — Practical parent
items.cue: Who has influenced you?
items.model: My father has influenced the way I deal with problems. He usually starts by asking what we can do next, even when something has gone wrong. I remember missing a bus as a teenager and expecting a long lecture. Instead, he helped me work out another route, and we talked about planning afterwards. I try to use that same calm, practical approach now.
expressions: deal with problems = respond to difficulties
work out = find a solution
that same approach = a similar way of responding

challenge.cue: Have you told them?
challenge.model: Yes, I told him about that memory recently. He didn't remember the exact day, but he was glad that his response had helped me.

items.title: Who has influenced you? — Supportive colleague
items.cue: Who has influenced you?
items.model: A former colleague influenced me when I was new at work. She explained things clearly, but she didn't take over every time I struggled. Once, she talked me through a difficult phone call and then let me try the next one myself. I admired that balance of support and trust. Now, when I help someone, I try to give them room to work things out too.
expressions: take over = do the task instead of someone
talked me through = explained step by step
work things out = find answers through thinking

challenge.cue: Have you told them?
challenge.model: Yes, I sent her a message when I moved to another role. I wanted her to know that the small things she did had stayed with me.

items.title: What is a useful habit you have? — Original website example
items.cue: What is a useful habit you have?
items.model: A useful habit I have is preparing tomorrow’s first task before I stop work. It makes starting the next morning much easier.
expressions: One habit that helps me is…
I usually do it when…
It helps because…

challenge.cue: Was it difficult to build?

items.title: What is a useful habit you have? — Preparing tomorrow
items.cue: What is a useful habit you have?
items.model: One useful habit I have is preparing the first task for tomorrow before I finish work. I leave a short note and open the document I'll need. It helps because I don't start the morning wondering where to begin. To keep the habit manageable, I spend only a couple of minutes on it. If I forget one day, I simply do it the next evening.
expressions: one useful habit I have is = one regular action that helps me is
where to begin = what to do first
a couple of minutes = about two minutes

challenge.cue: Was it difficult to build?
challenge.model: Remembering was difficult at first. I added a reminder near the end of my workday until the action became more familiar.

items.title: What is a useful habit you have? — Short evening walk
items.cue: What is a useful habit you have?
items.model: I usually take a short walk after dinner. It gives me a clear break between the busy part of the day and the evening. I often leave my phone in my pocket and notice what's happening around me. I keep the walk short enough that it doesn't feel like a big task. If it's raining, I choose another small activity that helps me pause.
expressions: a clear break between = a distinct pause separating
around me = in my surroundings
short enough that = brief enough to avoid a problem

challenge.cue: Was it difficult to build?
challenge.model: It was easier once I connected it to dinner. I didn't have to choose a new time every day, which helped me remember.

items.title: What is a useful habit you have? — Recording useful phrases
items.cue: What is a useful habit you have?
items.model: I keep a small note of useful English phrases I hear. When a phrase seems relevant to my life, I write one personal example rather than copying a long list. I usually do this after watching a short video. Later, I try to use one phrase in a spoken answer. Keeping the list small makes it easier to return to and actually practise.
expressions: relevant to my life = useful in my own situations
rather than copying = instead of reproducing
return to = use or review again

challenge.cue: Was it difficult to build?
challenge.model: The difficult part was stopping myself from collecting too much. I had to learn to choose phrases I was likely to use soon.

items.title: Describe your current project. — Original website example
items.cue: Describe your current project.
items.model: My current project is improving account setup. We are simplifying the steps and testing whether new users understand what to do next.
expressions: The project is about…
My role is…
Right now…

challenge.cue: What decision is coming next?

items.title: Describe your current project. — Website project overview
items.cue: Describe your current project.
items.model: The project is about making our shop's website easier for new customers to use. My role is to review the ordering steps and suggest clearer wording. We've already identified a few confusing parts and prepared an early version of the changes. Right now, we're deciding what to test first. The next milestone is to watch a few people try the updated process and learn where they still need help.
expressions: the project is about = the purpose of the work is
my role is to = my contribution is to
the next milestone is = the next important stage is

challenge.cue: What decision is coming next?
challenge.model: We need to decide which change to test first. I'd prefer the part that causes the most confusion, rather than the easiest cosmetic change.

items.title: Describe your current project. — Community event project
items.cue: Describe your current project.
items.model: I'm helping organise a small community book exchange. The idea is to give people a simple way to pass on books they've finished and discover something new. I'm responsible for the sign-up list and the table layout. We have a possible venue, but we're still checking how much space is available. Our next step is to confirm the date and explain how the exchange will work.
expressions: the idea is to = the purpose is to
responsible for = in charge of this task
we're still checking = we have not confirmed yet

challenge.cue: What decision is coming next?
challenge.model: We need to choose between a smaller indoor space and a larger outdoor one. The weather risk will be part of that decision.

items.title: Describe your current project. — Personal recipe collection
items.cue: Describe your current project.
items.model: My current project is making a small collection of family recipes. I want to record the dishes we cook often so I can make them more confidently myself. My role is to write down the ingredients and ask about steps that aren't usually measured. I've finished a few recipes and added photos. The next challenge is checking whether someone else can follow the instructions without extra explanation.
expressions: my current project is = the work I am doing now is
write down = record in words
without extra explanation = without needing more guidance

challenge.cue: What decision is coming next?
challenge.model: I need to decide which recipe to test next. I'll probably choose a simple dish so I can focus on whether the instructions are clear.

items.title: What are you looking forward to? — Original website example
items.cue: What are you looking forward to?
items.model: I’m looking forward to finishing my current project and taking a short trip. Both feel like a good reward after a busy few months.
expressions: I’m looking forward to…
It matters to me because…
Before then, I need to…

challenge.cue: What are you doing to prepare?

items.title: What are you looking forward to? — Family visit
items.cue: What are you looking forward to?
items.model: I'm looking forward to visiting my grandparents next month. We talk on the phone, but I haven't spent a full day with them for a while. I'd like to have lunch together and hear more of their stories. Before then, I need to arrange my travel and check which day suits them. I'm hoping to keep the visit relaxed rather than packing in lots of activities.
expressions: I'm looking forward to = I feel happy about a future event
for a while = for some time
which day suits them = which day is convenient for them

challenge.cue: What are you doing to prepare?
challenge.model: I'm checking the travel options and asking what they would enjoy doing. I'd rather plan around their energy than arrive with a busy schedule.

items.title: What are you looking forward to? — Finishing a course
items.cue: What are you looking forward to?
items.model: I'm looking forward to finishing my evening course in a few weeks. I've enjoyed it, but combining lessons with work has made the days quite full. It matters to me because I want to see the result of the effort I've put in. Before the final session, I need to complete one assignment and review my notes. Afterwards, I'd like a quiet weekend to rest.
expressions: combining lessons with work = managing study and employment together
effort I've put in = work I have done
before the final session = before the last lesson

challenge.cue: What are you doing to prepare?
challenge.model: I've divided the assignment into smaller tasks and set aside a little time each evening. That should help me avoid a last-minute rush.

items.title: What are you looking forward to? — Trying a new activity
items.cue: What are you looking forward to?
items.model: I'm looking forward to a beginner photography workshop this weekend. I've been taking pictures on my phone for a while, but I'd like to understand what makes some images work better than others. I'm also hoping to meet people with a similar interest. Before then, I need to choose a few photos to bring and check where the class is held.
expressions: for a while = for some time
similar interest = enjoyment of the same topic
before then = before that future time

challenge.cue: What are you doing to prepare?
challenge.model: I'm choosing three photos I like and one I'm unsure about. That will give me something specific to ask the teacher.

items.title: Where do you see yourself in five years? — Original website example
items.cue: Where do you see yourself in five years?
items.model: In five years, I hope to lead a thoughtful product team. I want to stay close to customers while helping other designers grow.
expressions: In five years, I hope to…
I’d like to be someone who…
To move in that direction…

challenge.cue: What could change that plan?

items.title: Where do you see yourself in five years? — Professional growth
items.cue: Where do you see yourself in five years?
items.model: In five years, I hope to have more responsibility at work and feel comfortable guiding a small team. I don't have a particular job title in mind. I'd like to be someone who explains things clearly and helps others do good work. To move in that direction, I'm improving my communication and asking to join projects where I can learn from more experienced colleagues.
expressions: in five years, I hope to = my future aim is to
in mind = as a specific idea
move in that direction = make progress towards that goal

challenge.cue: What could change that plan?
challenge.model: A different interest or a change in family needs could affect the plan. I'd still want to keep learning, even if the role changed.

items.title: Where do you see yourself in five years? — Independent everyday life
items.cue: Where do you see yourself in five years?
items.model: In five years, I'd like to feel more settled and independent. I hope to have a routine that gives me time for work, family and my own interests. I'd also like to use English comfortably in everyday situations, including when I travel. I'm working towards that by building small habits now. I can't predict exactly where I'll live or work, but I know how I'd like life to feel.
expressions: I'd like to feel = the state I hope for is
working towards that = taking steps to achieve it
can't predict exactly = do not know for certain

challenge.cue: What could change that plan?
challenge.model: Work opportunities or family responsibilities might change the details. I'd try to keep the same priorities even if the timetable became different.

items.title: Where do you see yourself in five years? — Exploring a future career
items.cue: Where do you see yourself in five years?
items.model: I'm still exploring my options, so I don't have a fixed picture of five years from now. I hope to be doing work that suits my strengths and gives me opportunities to learn. I'd like to be more confident making decisions and explaining my ideas. For now, I'm trying different projects and talking to people about their work, so my next choices are based on real experience.
expressions: exploring my options = considering possible choices
suits my strengths = fits what I do well
for now = at this stage

challenge.cue: What could change that plan?
challenge.model: A project that I unexpectedly enjoy could change my direction. I want to stay open to that while still taking useful steps now.
